openTomorrow: Yes, I'd open it tomorrow. I deliberately missed today to test the freeze feature and see how the app handles streaks. Now I'm curious to see if using the freeze actually works and if I can get back on track without losing everything.
secured: Secured means I've completed the daily challenge and locked in that day's progress toward my streak. It's like confirming that I showed up and did the work.
freeze: A freeze is a safety net for when you miss a day. It lets you skip one missed day without breaking your streak, but you can only use it if you actually missed exactly one day. I have one left and can earn another at 7 days.
selfReported: Self-reported means I'm telling the app myself that I completed the challenge for the day, rather than it tracking something automatically like steps or workouts.
best: The best moment was realizing the app has a freeze feature built in. It makes missing a day feel less like failure and more like I have a safety buffer. That's actually smart design.
worst: The worst moment was seeing that zero on my streak counter. Even though I did it intentionally to test things, that visual hit harder than I expected. It definitely makes you not want to miss days.
tellFriend: I'd tell them: 'Try GRIIT if you want to build a real habit with actual consequences. It's not just about logging—it feels like you're actually accountable. Fair warning though: that broken streak will mess with your head.'
